title: Items list leaks other users' items (owner filter removed for non-superusers)
suspect_detail: read_items(), non-superuser else-branch: the diff removed `.where(Item.owner_id == current_user.id)` from both the count query and the item select
root_cause: The regression diff dropped the owner_id filter in the non-superuser branch of GET /items/. Any authenticated user now gets every user's items, and `count` is the global total.
rationale: This is a data leak and an authorization failure, not a policy change. The endpoint's single-item routes (read, update, delete) still enforce ownership with 403, so the list route is now inconsistent with them. The UI test TC-043 fails for the same reason. User B sees A's item, so the empty state 'You don't have any items yet' never renders. The frontend code is correct and only displays what the API returns. No test change is warranted.
steps: As A, create 2 items; as B, create 1 item
In the UI, log in as a new user B with no items and open /items
expected: A receives only A's 2 items with count=2. A user with no items sees the empty state.
actual: A receives all users' items (extra IDs present) and the count is the global total. User B sees A's items, so the empty state is never shown.

title: Sign-up minimum password length raised from 8 to 10 characters
root_cause: The diff changed UserRegister.password min_length from 8 to 10, so an 8-character sign-up password now returns 422.
rationale: The change looks like a deliberate tightening of password policy rather than a defect. A stricter minimum is a common, sensible change, and nothing else is broken. It is not certain, though. The change is inconsistent with UserCreate, UpdatePassword, NewPassword and UserUpdate, which still use min_length=8, so it may be an accidental or partial change. A human should confirm the intended policy. If 10 is the intent, update TC-005 (boundary 10 accepted, 9 rejected, 128 accepted, 129 rejected) and align the other schemas. If not, revert to 8.
steps: Compare with the plan: 8 and 128 characters should be accepted, 129 rejected
expected: 8-char password returns 200 (per the plan and the previous behaviour).
actual: 422 Unprocessable Content, because the minimum is now 10.
